stage.title: Implement transient and global resource reuse

goal: Add frame-local transient resource aliasing and constrained global resource pooling after the barrier compiler can prove lifetimes and emit alias barriers.
entry_gate: The barrier and queue synchronization checkpoint can derive resource lifetimes and hazards.
Compiled barriers can express aliasing and queue ownership boundaries.
External import/export resources have explicit lifetime and state boundaries.

hard_rules.rule: Do not pool imported external resources.
Do not globally pool sampled-only textures, depth textures, upload buffers, readback buffers, acceleration structures, or bindless backing buffers.
Global ResourcePool reuse is limited to color attachments, UAV textures, and UAV buffers.
Do not alias resources whose live intervals overlap after queue synchronization expansion.
Do not collapse global ResourcePool and frame-local transient aliasing into one allocator. Global pooling owns cross-frame physical reuse; transient allocation owns single-frame logical aliasing.
Do not force canonical transitions on global pool return. Store final known state and compile checkout transition or discard first-use transition instead.

Do not let external native passes or multiple RenderGraph instances borrow pooled resources unless pool checkout can prove completion, owner queue, last state, native interop capability, and descriptor lifetime.

checkpoints.title: Compile resource lifetime intervals
checkpoints.problem: Transient allocation cannot be correct until the graph knows first use, last use, queue-expanded lifetime, export lifetime, and alias barriers.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Each transient resource has a compiled first-use and last-use pass index per queue segment.
Cross-queue handoffs extend lifetime until the consumer queue completes the relevant acquire/use interval.
Exported resources remain live through their declared final state publication.
Imported resources are excluded from transient allocation.

checkpoints.title: Implement TransientResourceAllocator
checkpoints.problem: Frame-local resources should be reused inside one compiled graph instead of being created and destroyed per pass.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Allocator groups compatible transient texture and buffer descriptors.
Allocator assigns physical resources only to non-overlapping lifetime intervals.
Alias barriers are inserted when one physical resource backs multiple logical resources in one frame.
Transient resources are retired at the frame boundary and never escape through user handles.
Transient allocator records physical slots separately from global pool checkout so single-frame aliasing and cross-frame reuse remain independent.

checkpoints.title: Implement constrained ResourcePool
checkpoints.problem: Some resources should survive across frames for allocation efficiency, but unconstrained global pooling creates stale state, layout, and lifetime bugs.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: ResourcePool accepts only color attachment textures, UAV textures, and UAV buffers.
Pool keys include size, format, usage flags, sample count, mip/array shape, memory class, sharing mode, backend allocation compatibility flags, and native interop capability flags.
Pool checkout returns resources with stored last known state and owner queue metadata.
Compile emits checkout first-use transition from stored state, or discard transition when the first use fully overwrites the resource.
Pool return is delayed until the RHIExecutor completion boundary proves the last GPU use is retired.
Pool return records final whole-resource state instead of eagerly transitioning to a canonical state.
Global ResourcePool is device-owned and independent from graph-local transient allocator state.

checkpoints.title: Integrate reuse with external imports and bindless updates
checkpoints.problem: Resource reuse must not invalidate bindless descriptors or external references that outlive a frame-local graph.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Transient resources cannot be allocated into bindless arrays that outlive the graph unless the graph owns descriptor update and invalidation lifetime.
Imported resources are never placed in the transient allocator or global ResourcePool.
Global pooled resources are unbound or rebound only through explicit graph-owned descriptor update passes.
External native passes can touch pooled resources only when the pool key includes compatible native handle and synchronization capabilities.
Pool retirement cannot race worker-thread record, external pass completion, or RHI translate.

checkpoints.title: Add focused reuse validation cases
checkpoints.problem: Aliasing and pooling bugs often appear as later-frame corruption, so focused tests must verify reuse rules and retirement boundaries.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Tests cover non-overlapping transient aliasing, overlapping lifetime rejection, alias barriers, pool checkout canonical state, and delayed pool return.
Tests cover rejection of unsupported global pool resource categories.
Tests run through existing repository scripts.

stage_exit_gate: Frame-local transient resources reuse memory safely through compiled lifetime intervals.
Global ResourcePool reuse is constrained to the allowed resource categories only.
Global ResourcePool and transient alias allocator have separate responsibilities and metadata.
External native access and multiple RenderGraph instances use completion-checked global pool checkout, not cross-graph transient aliasing.
Pool return and alias reuse are ordered by RHIExecutor completion boundaries.
validation: Run testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 after focused reuse tests land.
Run testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1 after the stage-sized landing.
